action_criteria.expected_evidence: Serum anti-GluN1 IgG positive (titer 1:80), read with the CSF; profound hyponatremia (sodium 122 mEq/L); thyroid, neuronal-surface and onconeural antibodies negative
action_criteria.label: Obtain the serum work-up: blood count, chemistry, thyroid function and antibodies, HIV, beta-hCG and a cell-based serum anti-GluN1 IgG assay read together with the CSF result
action_criteria.rationale: Screens metabolic, endocrine, infectious and pregnancy-related contributors and pairs the serum antibody with the decisive CSF assay; here it uncovers profound hyponatremia.

action_criteria.expected_evidence: Subtle left medial temporal FLAIR hyperintensity without restricted diffusion, hemorrhage or enhancement; no structural lesion
action_criteria.label: Obtain contrast-enhanced brain MRI to exclude HSV encephalitis, structural lesions and overlapping demyelination; a normal MRI does not exclude anti-NMDAR encephalitis
action_criteria.rationale: Excludes HSV encephalitis, structural lesions and overlapping demyelination before LP; it is normal in most patients and does not confirm the diagnosis.

action_criteria.expected_evidence: Mild lymphocytic pleocytosis (12 cells/uL) with borderline IgG index; HSV-1/2 PCR negative; CSF IgG anti-GluN1 positive (titer 1:128)
action_criteria.label: Analyze CSF for cells, protein and glucose, oligoclonal bands or IgG index, HSV PCR and a cell-based IgG anti-GluN1 assay
action_criteria.rationale: The CSF anti-GluN1 cell-based assay is the decisive test (Graus 2016 definite criteria), and HSV PCR addresses the infectious mimic that must not be missed.

action_criteria.expected_evidence: Diffuse slowing with frontal rhythmic delta, left temporal sharp waves and one left temporal electroclinical seizure; no extreme delta brush
action_criteria.label: Obtain an EEG for encephalopathic and epileptiform abnormalities, including extreme delta brush
action_criteria.rationale: An abnormal EEG is one of the Graus 2016 supporting findings, and the witnessed staring spells need electrographic characterization.

action_criteria.expected_evidence: Left ovarian 1.2 cm complex cystic lesion with shadowing calcification, consistent with a mature cystic teratoma
action_criteria.label: Screen for an ovarian teratoma with pelvic and abdominal ultrasound
action_criteria.rationale: Women of reproductive age carry the highest teratoma risk; tumor removal is part of first-line treatment.

action_criteria.expected_evidence: Seizure burden and evolution of the background over 24 hours or more
action_criteria.label: Escalate to continuous EEG to quantify seizure burden while consciousness fluctuates or seizures persist
action_criteria.rationale: The routine EEG captured a seizure and she has recurrent staring spells, so a 30-minute record underestimates the seizure burden.

action_criteria.expected_evidence: Serum osmolality 254 mOsm/kg with urine osmolality 486 mOsm/kg and urine sodium 54 mmol/L
action_criteria.label: Measure serum and urine osmolality (with urine sodium) to characterize the hyponatremia
action_criteria.rationale: Sodium below 130 mEq/L needs its own work-up; low serum osmolality with inappropriately concentrated urine and urine sodium above 30 mmol/L defines SIADH before fluid restriction or hypertonic saline.

action_criteria.expected_evidence: Sertraline as a contributor to the low sodium; estrogen-containing contraceptive and IVIG thrombosis risk
action_criteria.label: Check the patient's medications against the drugs the acute plan needs (acyclovir, corticosteroids, IVIG, antiseizure medication)
action_criteria.rationale: No interaction here changes the first-line plan; the check confirms the sertraline and contraceptive issues before prescribing.

action_criteria.expected_evidence: General published evidence on anti-NMDAR encephalitis diagnosis and immunotherapy
action_criteria.label: Optionally review published evidence on anti-NMDAR encephalitis diagnosis and immunotherapy
action_criteria.rationale: Background reading only; no diagnostic or management step depends on it.

prohibited_recommendations: Do not give haloperidol or other high-potency D2 antagonists for agitation: patients with anti-NMDAR encephalitis are prone to severe extrapyramidal and neuroleptic-malignant-like reactions.
Do not delay immunotherapy while waiting for the anti-NMDAR antibody result when clinical probability is high: antibody turnaround can take 1-2 weeks and delay worsens outcome.
Do not attribute the presentation to a primary psychiatric disorder while seizures, dyskinesias, autonomic instability, an abnormal EEG or CSF inflammation remain unexplained.
Do not perform lumbar puncture without prior imaging in a patient with altered consciousness, focal signs, or new seizures: exclude mass effect first.
Do not interpret a negative serum anti-NMDAR antibody as ruling out the disease; the CSF assay is the gold standard and may be positive when serum is negative.
required_recommendations: Start IV acyclovir 10 mg/kg every 8 hours at presentation, and stop it once CSF HSV PCR is negative and the antibody diagnosis is established; repeat the PCR on a second CSF sample if the first LP was within 72 hours of onset and HSV encephalitis remains plausible.

Start first-line immunotherapy without waiting for the antibody result once infection is reasonably excluded: IV methylprednisolone 1 g daily for 5 days with IVIG 0.4 g/kg/day for 5 days (2 g/kg total) or plasma exchange (5 to 7 exchanges).
Arrange prompt surgical removal of the left ovarian teratoma (laparoscopic, ovary-sparing where feasible) as part of first-line treatment, with gynecology.

Treat seizures with an antiseizure medication such as levetiracetam (already started at 500 mg twice daily; titrate) or lacosamide; avoid valproate in a woman able to become pregnant; seizures respond mainly to immunotherapy.
Monitor with continuous EEG for non-convulsive seizures while consciousness fluctuates or seizures persist.
Admit to a neurology high-dependency or neurocritical care bed for hypertonic saline with frequent serum sodium checks, seizure precautions and continuous cardiac monitoring.

If there is no meaningful clinical improvement 10 to 14 days after first-line therapy, escalate to rituximab (375 mg/m² weekly for 4 doses or 1 g twice 2 weeks apart, after hepatitis B screening) and/or cyclophosphamide; discuss fertility preservation before cyclophosphamide.
Treat agitation and insomnia with benzodiazepines (lorazepam) first.

Treat the profound hyponatremia (122 mEq/L) as SIADH after review of sertraline (dose recently increased; withhold it while sodium is low): fluid restriction and, because of the seizures, a 3% hypertonic saline bolus, correcting by no more than 10 mEq/L in 24 hours.
Neurology-led care with psychiatry for behavioral management; gynecology for the teratoma.

avoided_actions.rationale: Transthoracic echo is not indicated for anti-NMDAR encephalitis; it adds cost without informing diagnosis or management unless a discrete cardiac concern (e.g., new murmur, embolic stroke) coexists.
EMG/NCS plays no role in the diagnostic workup of anti-NMDAR encephalitis; it neither confirms the antibody-mediated CNS process nor distinguishes among the differential diagnoses.
Amyloid PET targets Alzheimer pathology and contributes no information to the diagnosis or treatment of autoimmune encephalitis in a young patient with subacute neuropsychiatric symptoms.

DaTscan evaluates nigrostriatal dopaminergic function and has no role in autoimmune encephalitis; the orofacial dyskinesias of anti-NMDAR encephalitis are antibody-mediated, not presynaptic dopaminergic.

differential.key_features: Serum neuronal-surface panel negative (LGI1, CASPR2, GABA-B, AMPA, DPPX) and onconeural antibodies negative; CSF anti-GluN1 positive.

Sodium 122 mEq/L after the sertraline increase can cause confusion and seizures, but the behavioral change began before the dose increase, and orofacial dyskinesias, CSF pleocytosis and CSF anti-GluN1 are not explained by it.
Seizures, orofacial dyskinesias, autonomic fluctuation, left temporal electrographic seizures and CSF pleocytosis are not explained by her anxiety disorder or a primary psychosis.
Mother has SLE and ANA is 1:80 speckled, a low titer common in healthy people; no rash, arthritis, serositis, cytopenia or renal involvement, and the CSF anti-GluN1 result accounts for the syndrome.

differential.key_features: No antipsychotic exposure; after the sertraline increase there is no clonus, temperature 38.0 C and CK 136 U/L (Hunter criteria not met); toxicology positive only for the prescribed benzodiazepine.

key_clinical_evidence: Three weeks of subacute behavioral and cognitive change, seizures, orofacial dyskinesias and autonomic fluctuation: four of the six Graus 2016 groups.
CSF IgG anti-GluN1 positive (titer 1:128) on cell-based assay: definite anti-NMDAR encephalitis (Graus 2016); serum positive (1:80) is read with the CSF.

MRI shows only subtle left medial temporal FLAIR signal without restricted diffusion or hemorrhage; MRI is normal or non-specific in about two thirds of patients and here excludes HSV encephalitis and structural causes.
EEG shows diffuse slowing with left temporal sharp waves and seizures; extreme delta brush is absent, which excludes nothing.
Pelvic ultrasound shows a 1.2 cm left ovarian mature cystic teratoma: its removal is part of first-line treatment. Profound hyponatremia (122 mEq/L, SIADH pattern) needs its own correction.
Earlier immunotherapy and tumor removal are associated with better outcome (Titulaer 2013).

red_herrings.correct_interpretation: Seizures, dyskinesias, autonomic instability, an abnormal EEG or CSF pleocytosis alongside the psychiatric change mandate exclusion of anti-NMDAR encephalitis before a psychiatric diagnosis is accepted.
red_herrings.data_point: Acute psychiatric presentation (insomnia, emotional lability, paranoid ideation) in a young woman with generalized anxiety disorder, first managed by her psychiatrist.
red_herrings.intended_effect: Anchors the agent on a primary psychiatric diagnosis (first-episode psychosis, brief psychotic disorder) and delays neurologic workup.

red_herrings.correct_interpretation: Hyponatremia occurs in anti-NMDAR encephalitis but is more typical of anti-LGI1 encephalitis; it needs its own work-up and correction and does not point away from the diagnosis. Here the recent sertraline increase may contribute.
red_herrings.intended_effect: Tempts the agent toward a primary metabolic-encephalopathy framing (SIADH from another cause, dehydration, polydipsia) instead of recognizing SIADH as a known complication of NMDAR-E.

red_herrings.correct_interpretation: NMS requires antipsychotic exposure with lead-pipe rigidity, hyperthermia and markedly elevated CK; a CK of 136 U/L reflects seizures and dyskinesias and does not change management.
red_herrings.intended_effect: Raises concern for neuroleptic malignant syndrome or rhabdomyolysis when combined with dyskinesias and hyperthermia.

contraindications: Haloperidol and other high-potency D2 antagonists: class warning for severe extrapyramidal and neuroleptic-malignant-like reactions in suspected autoimmune encephalitis.
interactions: Sertraline: SSRIs are associated with SIADH and hyponatremia; review the indication and dose when serum sodium is low.
Ethinylestradiol (combined oral contraceptive) with IVIG: estrogen use is a listed risk factor for IVIG-associated thrombosis; ensure hydration and the slowest practical infusion rate.
Ethinylestradiol with methylprednisolone: estrogens reduce corticosteroid clearance; effect modest at pulse doses.
Lorazepam with other sedatives: additive CNS and respiratory depression.
Albuterol with high-dose methylprednisolone: additive hypokalemia; monitor potassium.
Levetiracetam: no clinically relevant pharmacokinetic interaction with the current medicines; behavioral adverse effects (irritability, mood change) are recognized.
Acyclovir: no interaction with the current medicines; dose by renal function and maintain hydration.

anti-NMDA receptor encephalitis diagnosi.query: anti-NMDA receptor encephalitis diagnosis and treatment

results.finding: Definite anti-NMDAR encephalitis requires one or more of six major symptom groups and IgG anti-GluN1 antibodies, with CSF testing included; probable disease requires four groups (or three with a teratoma) of rapid onset plus an abnormal EEG or CSF pleocytosis or oligoclonal bands.
results.source: Graus F et al. Lancet Neurol 2016;15:391-404

results.finding: All patients had antibodies in CSF, whereas about 14% were negative in serum; CSF titers related more closely to outcome than serum titers.
results.source: Gresa-Arribas N et al. Lancet Neurol 2014;13:167-177

results.finding: 38% had a tumor, mostly ovarian teratoma; 53% improved within 4 weeks of first-line immunotherapy or tumor removal; second-line rituximab or cyclophosphamide after first-line failure was associated with better outcome; 81% had mRS 0-2 at 24 months.
results.source: Titulaer MJ et al. Lancet Neurol 2013;12:157-165

results.finding: Extreme delta brush was found in 7 of 23 adults with anti-NMDA receptor encephalitis and was associated with a more prolonged illness.
Severe intolerance to antipsychotics (rigidity, hyperthermia, rhabdomyolysis, neuroleptic-malignant-like reactions) was frequent in patients with anti-NMDA receptor encephalitis who received them.
results.source: Lejuste F et al. Neurol Neuroimmunol Neuroinflamm 2016;3:e280

anti-NMDA receptor encephalitis diagnosi.summary: Published criteria and cohort data on anti-NMDA receptor encephalitis: definite diagnosis rests on CSF IgG anti-GluN1 antibodies; first-line immunotherapy and tumor removal are followed by second-line agents when there is no response.

patient.history_present_illness: This 28-year-old right-handed woman is brought to the emergency department by her husband with progressive confusion, behavioral changes, and a witnessed seizure. Approximately three weeks ago, her husband noticed she was sleeping poorly, lying awake for most of the night despite no change in her routine or medication. Over the following days, she became increasingly irritable and emotionally labile, crying without provocation and expressing paranoid ideation that her coworkers were trying to get her fired. She called in sick to work repeatedly and stopped exercising. Her husband initially attributed the changes to stress, as work had been demanding. Ten days prior to this presentation, she was evaluated at an urgent care and referred to her psychiatrist, who increased her sertraline to 100 mg daily and prescribed lorazepam 0.5 mg as needed for acute anxiety. Despite this, her behavior continued to deteriorate. She began having difficulty following conversations, frequently losing her train of thought mid-sentence, and on several occasions she was found staring blankly for 10-15 seconds before resuming activity, which she could not recall. Five days ago, her husband witnessed a generalized tonic-clonic seizure lasting approximately 60 seconds while she was sitting on the couch. He called 911, and she was taken to a community hospital emergency department where a CT head was unremarkable. She was given a loading dose of levetiracetam 1500 mg IV and discharged with a prescription for levetiracetam 500 mg twice daily and instructions to follow up with neurology. Over the next four days, her confusion worsened substantially. She became unable to manage simple household tasks, left the stove on twice, and had difficulty recognizing familiar neighborhood landmarks while being driven. Her husband also noticed unusual repetitive mouth movements that she seemed unaware of. Today, she became acutely agitated, was found attempting to leave the house in her pajamas in the rain, and did not recognize her own mother who had come to help. Her husband brought her to this tertiary care emergency department for further evaluation. He denies any recent fevers, headaches, or focal weakness. There is no history of head trauma, recent travel, tick exposure, or new sexual contacts. Her psychiatric history is limited to anxiety managed with low-dose sertraline; she has never been hospitalized for psychiatric illness and has no prior psychotic episodes.

neurological_exam.additional: Intermittent perioral and lingual dyskinesias are observed, including subtle lip-pursing and tongue movements. These are initially attributed to anxiety by the referring psychiatrist. One episode of behavioral arrest with staring, lip smacking, and right hand automatisms lasting approximately 20 seconds is witnessed during the examination, followed by brief post-ictal confusion superimposed on baseline encephalopathy. Mild diaphoresis is noted. Heart rate fluctuates between 88 and 115 bpm during the encounter.
neurological_exam.coordination: Finger-to-nose testing shows mild bilateral dysmetria, though this may be confounded by inattention. Heel-to-shin testing is grossly intact on the right; the patient does not cooperate with left-sided testing.
neurological_exam.cranial_nerves: Pupils equal and reactive, 3 mm bilaterally. Extraocular movements are full without nystagmus. Facial sensation is intact. There is subtle intermittent perioral twitching observed during examination, initially thought to be anxiety-related. Hearing is grossly intact bilaterally. Palate elevates symmetrically. Tongue is midline without fasciculations.
neurological_exam.gait: Unsteady, wide-based gait. The patient requires assistance and tends to veer to the left. Tandem gait is not attempted due to safety concerns.
neurological_exam.mental_status: Alert but confused. Oriented to person only; unable to state the date, month, or current location. Speech is fluent but tangential with occasional loose associations. She intermittently becomes agitated and attempts to get out of bed. Attention is impaired; unable to spell WORLD backward or perform serial 7s. Short-term memory is significantly impaired; recalls 0 of 3 objects at 5 minutes. She intermittently appears to respond to internal stimuli, though it is unclear whether these represent hallucinations or brief seizures. Montreal Cognitive Assessment score estimated at 12/30 based on partial cooperation.
neurological_exam.motor: Tone is mildly increased in bilateral upper extremities. Strength is 5/5 in all extremities when the patient cooperates, though she is intermittently resistive and effort is inconsistent. No pronator drift is observed. Occasional involuntary flexion posturing of the left wrist is noted during periods of inattention.
neurological_exam.reflexes: Biceps 2+ bilaterally, triceps 2+ bilaterally, brachioradialis 2+ bilaterally, patellar 3+ bilaterally (brisk), Achilles 2+ bilaterally. Plantar responses are flexor bilaterally. No clonus.
neurological_exam.sensory: Intact to light touch and pinprick in all extremities. Proprioception is intact at the great toes bilaterally. Detailed sensory examination is limited by the patient's fluctuating cooperation.
